DILG BACONC PIUANAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO 08 MR. ARJEN ABRAHAMSE Chairman Boskalis Philippines, Inc. Brgy. San Antonio, Ortigas City kristine.ann.andres@boskalis.com Dear Mr. Abrahamse: This has reference to your email dated 28 June 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion and clarifications on Section 7.A.02. of Municipal Ordinance No. 50, Administrative Code of Municipality of Bulakan, Bulacan, which concerns the employees yearly medical examination, viz: Section 7.4.02: EMPLOYEES YEARLY MEDICAL EXAMINATION - All Employees and workers of offices and factories are ordered to undergo yearly medical examination(s) and are required to secure (a) medical. certificate from the Municipal Health Officer to determine their physical fitness and health condition. Per your letter, you claim that Municipal Ordinance No. 50 is very general in its approach and does not have IRR or proper guidelines and that Memo Circ. No. 2023- 126 is vague in application and has no legal basis to require Mayor's Clearance. Additionally, Boskalis' strict compliance with the annual medical examinations and pre- employment examinations required by the Department of Labor and Employment. Hence, your request for opinion wherein you raised four issues, to wit: 1. Whether all employees are required to undergo Annual Medical Examination and secure a medical certificate from the Municipal Health Office despite compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Standards as amended. 2. Whether or not PESO is mandated under the law to enforce a Memorandum issued by the Office of the Mayor such as the Memorandum No. 2023-126 and require employers such as Boskalis to comply with the said memorandum. 3. Whether Section 7.A.02. Employees Yearly Medical Examination of Municipal Ordinance No. 50, Administrative Code of Municipality of Bulakan, Bulacan is in compliance with the Guidelines for Processing Business Permits, Related Clearances and Licenses in all Cities and Municipalities, Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 01 Series of 2021? 4. What is the legal basis for securing the Work Permit for all employees and workers in Bulakan? "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Allow us to first address the fourth issue directly as the other three issues are closely related to it. The Municipality of Bulakan's policy of requiring employees within its territorial jurisdiction to secure work permits is an exercise of police power. This is a delegated power to local government units (LGUs) and is the legal basis behind the subject regulation. This power of the LGU is bolstered by the constitutionally granted local autonomy enunciated under Article X, Section 2, of the 1987 Philippine Constitution. Consequently, Section 22, of RA. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 vests on every LGU, as a public corporation, the power to "exercise such other powers as are granted to corporations, subject to the limitations provided in this Code and other laws". In addition, the same section states that LGUs shall "enjoy full autonomy in the exercise of their proprietary functions, subject to the limitations provided in this Code and other applicable laws. Sec 22. Corporate Powers - (a) Every local government unit, as a corporation, shall have the following powers: (I) To have continuous succession in its corporate name; (2) To sue and be sued; (3) To have and use a corporate seal; (4) To acquire and convey real or personal property; (5) To enter into contracts; and (6) To exercise such other powers as are granted to corporations, subject to the limitations provided in this Code and other laws. (b) Local government units may continue using, modify, or change their existing corporate seals: Provided, That newly established local government units or those without corporate seals may create their own corporate seals which shall be registered with the Department of the Interior and Local Govemment: Provided, further, That any change of corporate seal shall also be registered as provided hereon. (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concemed. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. (d) Local government units shall enjoy full autonomy in the exercise of their proprietary functions and in the limitations provided in this Code and other applicable laws. The implementation of said regulation is pursuant to Section 7.A.02., on Employees Yearly Medical Examination, of Municipal Ordinance No. 50, the Administrative Code of the Municipality of Bulakan, Bulacan. Considering the jurisprudentially settled presumption of validity accorded to local legislative enactments, the implementation Page 2 of 4

by the Local Chief Executive (LCE) of Municipal Ordinance No. 50 is valid and legally sound. Having laid down the legal basis of the Municipal Regulation being implemented; we now proceed to address the 1st three queries. We discuss succinctly. As mentioned above, it has been well-recognized by law and jurisprudence that ordinances, like laws, enjoy a presumption of validity. Comparing this to Rule 1967.03 of the Occupational Health and Safety (OSH) Standards issued by the Department of Labor and Employment, it cannot be said that the two laws contradict each other. In essence, the municipal ordinance supports the DOLE's mandate of promoting safety in the workplace by adding two more requirements which are within the ambit of its power to do so. 1967.03: Periodic Annual Medical Examinations - Periodic annual medical examinations shall be conducted in order to follow-up previous findings, to allow early detection of occupational and non-occupational diseases and determine the effect of exposure of employees to health hazards. Lastly, it also promotes the General Welfare Clause provided in Rep. Act No. 7160. Section 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective govemance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local govemment units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. Based on the foregoing, we answer Query No. 1 in the affirmative. All employees are required to undergo Annual Medical Examination and secure a medical certificate from the Municipal Health Office despite their employer's compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Standards. As to Query No. 2, it appears that the Public Employment Services Office (PESO) is sanctioned to comply with the LCE's implementation of Municipal Ordinance No. 50 as it was duly enacted by the Sanggunian Bayan of Bulakan, Bulacan. The LCE is duty bound to enforce and implement said ordinance pursuant to Section 444 (b)(2) of the LGC, to wit: Page 3 of 4

"Section 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - xxx (2) Enforce all laws and ordinances relative to the governance of the municipality and the exercise of its corporate powers provided for under Section 22 of this Code implement all approved policies, programs, projects, services and activities of the municipality and, xxx" The PESO, being an office under the direct supervision of the executive department of the local government, the Office of the LCE, its implementation of Municipal Ordinance No. 50 is likewise authorized and proper. As to your third query, you are asking whether Section 7.A.02. of Municipal Ordinance No. 50, Administrative Code of Municipality of Bulakan, Bulacan, is in compliance with the Guidelines for Processing Business Permits, Related Clearances and Licenses in all Cities and Municipalities, Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 01 Series of 2021. We submit that we cannot provide a categorical answer to this. Instead, we submit that ARTA-DTI-DILG-DCT JMC No. 1 Series of 2021 is procedural in nature. The policy direction under Item 7 thereof prescribes for the streamlined procedures in processing business permits and other related permits, clearances and authorization. On the other hand, we regard the policy requirement of the assailed Ordinance No. 50 of the Municipality of Bulakan, Bulacan, as substantive in nature. Ergo, it precedes the application of procedural requirements under ARTA-DTI-DILG-DCT JMC No. I Series of 2021. All substantive requirements pursuant to municipal regulations must be complied before the timeline and streamlined processes required under the subject JMC shall be made applicable. On a final note, Boskalis Phils. Inc. is encouraged to comply with the mandate of Municipal Ordinance No. 50. Given that municipal councils derive their legislative powers from Congress, their enactments and/or actions are accorded equal respect, unless expressly declared unconstitutional by the courts. This opinion is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, B THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN TOR R. LLAMAS Und r cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLAJJVRULLLS-LRALLD/jkka Page 4 of 4
